lines.trans: Where did the bottle of expensive cognac disappear to?
Honestly speaking, I don't know at all.
And who should know if not you?
Kostya, you need to be fired from your job immediately!
It definitely stood here, I remember myself.
So that fake repairman stole it.
What an insolent, vile thief!
This bottle costs huge money.
Excuse me, I will fix everything right now.
Where did you run so fast?
I will catch up with that thief and return the cognac!
Just you dare not bring it back!

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'bottle'.

examples.trans: With a bottle of wine in your hand?

examples.text: Пыталась? С бутылкой вина в руке?
examples.trans: You tried? With a bottle of wine in your hand?

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Давай работай быстрее, гости уже давно ждут заказ!
examples.trans: Come on, work faster, the guests have been waiting for their order for a long time!

вернуть.gloss: to give back, to get back

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to give back', forming an aspectual pair with 'возвращать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to get back') (money you spent) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты эти деньги через полгода вернёшь.
examples.trans: You'll get this money back in six months.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'thief' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('here') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('! = you'll see!') (emphasis) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
Secondary conversational sense ('that's it, done') (at the start of a sentence) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to speak', forming an aspectual pair with 'сказать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to speak, to talk') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

догнать.gloss: to catch up with, to catch

meanings.en: to catch up with, to overtake
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'гнать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to catch up with, to catch', paired with 'догонять'.

examples.trans: The chubby girl won't catch you.
Go ahead, I'll catch up with you.

examples.text: Толстая девочка тебя не догонит. А Лёля пойдёт с тобой на вечеринку.
examples.trans: The chubby girl won't catch you. And Lyolya will go to the party with you.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Secondary conversational sense ('owe') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: to a loved one, and at the start of letters
to a loved one, and at the start of letters

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.
Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'so'.
verb: Что это значит? = What does it mean?
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to excuse', forming an aspectual pair with 'извинять'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to excuse, to forgive') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.en: to fix, to correct, to put right
meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'править'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fix, to correct', paired with 'исправлять'.

examples.trans: Excuse us, we will fix everything.

examples.text: Ученик быстро исправил ошибку в тетради.
examples.trans: The pupil quickly corrected the mistake in his notebook.

examples.text: Да, вы знаете, это очень серьёзная операция. Мы всё исправим. До свидания!
examples.trans: Yes, you know, it is a very serious operation. We'll fix everything. Goodbye!

meanings.note: genitive also 'коньяку' (some cognac)

examples.trans: And you're drinking French cognac yourself.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'where'.

examples.trans: Wait, where are you two going?

meanings.note: Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'technician', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.text: Они совсем не похожи на настоящих мастеров.
examples.trans: They look nothing like real technicians.

examples.text: А какие признаки должны быть у мастеров?
examples.trans: And what signs should technicians have?

meanings.note: showing a lack of respect in a rude or aggressive manner

examples.trans: That was a very insolent act.
Be quiet right now, insolent rump!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'ago'.
Secondary conversational sense ('back, backwards') (шаг назад = a step back) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago!

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил! Я сам приказ подписывал!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago! I signed the order myself!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'медленно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('huge, enormous').

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

побежать.gloss: to start running, to run off

meanings.en: to break into a run, to run off
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'бежать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to start running, to run off', paired with 'бежать'.

examples.text: Схватил собачку в парке и побежал.
examples.trans: Grab the little dog in the park and run.
The boy quickly ran off home.

examples.text: Да это легко. Схватил собачку в парке и побежал.
examples.trans: Come on, it's easy. Grab the little dog in the park and run.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'mean', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: You are a despicable man, Borya!

examples.text: Ты ответишь за это подлое предательство.
examples.trans: You will answer for this vile betrayal.
Stepanych, you are a truly vile villain!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мнить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to remember'.

examples.trans: Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.en: to try, to taste (food or drink)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to try', forming an aspectual pair with 'пробовать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to try, to attempt') (+ infinitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Try the tea with bread rings.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'пасть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to disappear, vanish'.

examples.text: Аркадий, что делать будем? Самсонов пропал.
examples.trans: Arkady, what are we going to do? Samsonov is missing.

examples.text: Таня, а куда пропал твой бывший муж?
examples.trans: Tanya, and where did your former husband disappear to?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'work', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('job') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
+ instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'quite'.
Secondary conversational sense ('not at all') (совсем не) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тоить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to cost'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to be worth') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And how much does the console cost?

meanings.note: the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

examples.text: Стоять на месте, никто не выходит из кухни без разрешения!
examples.trans: Freeze right there, nobody leaves the kitchen without permission!

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('like that, so') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Secondary conversational sense ('exactly, precisely') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to fire', forming an aspectual pair with 'увольнять'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'красть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to steal', paired with 'красть'.

examples.text: Чтобы он вернул деньги, которые украл.
examples.trans: For him to give back the money he stole.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fake, counterfeit, false').

examples.text: У нас фальшивый кластер. Операция «Золотой ярд».
examples.trans: Ours is the fake cluster. Operation Golden Billion.

examples.text: Значит, этот фальшивый мастер украл его.
examples.trans: So that fake repairman stole it.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Do you want me to tell you honestly?

examples.text: Всё честно, Лёха. Взрослые не умеют ждать.
examples.trans: It's all fair, Lyokha. Grown-ups can't wait.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
